newsitem.title: UK: Strike takes toll on BA's July traffic. [CORRECTED 14:29 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Strike takes toll on BA's July traffic. [CORRECTED 14:29 GMT]

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Tuesday its passenger traffic in July fell 1.1 percent due to the three-day strike by cabin crew last month, with business and first class traffic down by nine percent and non-premium up by 0.2 percent (corrects from down).

Many flights were grounded by the strike but seats sold on the aircraft, which BA managed to get way last month, averaged 77.7 percent of capacity, a 0.2 percentage point drop on the load factor a year ago.
BA said that cargo traffic was also affected by the strike but was up 1.8 percent in terms of cargo tonne kilometres at 321 CTKs.
The airline warned yesterday that it reckoned the industrial dispute has already cost it 125 million pounds ($203.7 million) in lost profits this year.

Management negotiators are still locked in talks with the main cabin crew union, BASSA, in an effort to settle the dispute over plans to save 42 million pounds a year from restructuring cabin crew pay.
Both sides have agreed not to comment on the progress of the talks while they continue. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
